criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`: a test with a fake producer that edits files then times out shows the job closes timed_out and keeps a candidate (a commit, not only a work directory) whose diff holds those edits; the outcome reason or note names the kept candidate.
criteria.evidence: a_producer_that_hits_its_deadline_keeps_its_work_and_closes_timed_out passed. Reading the diff: the test reads candidate.json at the closing head and requires candidate_commit. It checks that the commit's parent is the base commit, that src/partial.rs and README.md in the commit hold the edits and differ from the base, and that the change list is exactly those two files. It also checks that the reason, outcome.json and the note contain the short commit, that no kept directory was made, and that check_history reports no violations.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`: a test retries that timed-out job and shows the next producer starts with the kept edits present and its brief names the earlier job id and the files already changed, plus what the plan still needs.
criteria.evidence: Both tests passed: retrying_a_timed_out_job_starts_from_the_kept_work_with_the_note and retrying_a_timed_out_job_whose_base_moved_starts_clean. The first checks that src/partial.rs is in the new working directory before the producer acts. It also checks that the brief contains '## Resume', the first job's id, 'kept as candidate <short>', src/partial.rs and README.md, and a 'Still to do' list with '> - CHANGELOG.md'.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: the whole suite passes, including the history check on the records of a timed-out job.
criteria.evidence: Athena's record shows `cargo test --locked` passed in CI for cc530d2b. The keep test asserts check_history() has no violations on the timed-out job's records. I also ran the core timeout unit tests (15 passed), including a_deadline_keeps_a_candidate_and_timeout_seed_prefers_it_to_the_kept_directory and the_timeout_note_names_the_candidate_the_changed_files_and_what_is_still_to_do.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Athena's records show both checks passed in CI run 41419187728 for cc530d2b.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry stating that a producer's work is kept when it reaches its deadline and that a retry resumes from it.
criteria.evidence: An entry under [Unreleased] / Changed begins: 'A producer's work is kept when it reaches its deadline, and `athena retry` resumes from it.' It goes on to describe the candidate commit, the reason wording, the Still to do list, the Resume brief, the fallbacks, and the root cause.

criteria.criterion: docs/decisions.md records the call (keep the candidate on deadline) as a new decision referencing D124 alternative c, with sources read.
criteria.evidence: D151 'A producer that reaches its deadline keeps its work as a candidate, and a retry resumes from it' cites D124 alternative (c). It has Case, Root cause, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, and Provenance sections; Provenance lists the files read, what was measured and what was not.

findings.summary: Two changed files are not on the expected deliverables list: run/candidate.rs and reading.rs.
findings.evidence: candidate.rs moves the commit-building code out of candidate_stage into build_candidate, so the deadline path reuses it; this file was in the planned files. reading.rs gains one line, `candidate: None`, in a test fixture so the new RetrySeed field compiles. Both changes are needed and small.

findings.summary: The change does not use the environment stop's resume mark, which the reading said it would.
findings.evidence: The reading said 'the same candidate and resume-mark mechanism an environment stop uses'. The change instead seeds the retry's producer through seed_commit, the path a retry of a rejected candidate uses. D151 explains why: a resume mark skips the producer and would send half-done work to the verifier. The request asks that 'the next producer run starts from that candidate', so this choice fits the request better than a literal reading would.

findings.summary: Retries of timed-out jobs can now have their readings refused, because the earlier job's candidate files must be listed or put out of scope.
findings.evidence: The test's scenario reading was changed to list README.md and src/partial.rs so the retry's reading is accepted. The changelog and D151 disclose this effect and say the refusal rate was not measured. Athena's replay found 0 of 50 accepted readings newly refused.

findings.summary: The kept candidate commit is not on any branch, so git garbage collection could remove it.
findings.evidence: Other candidates are kept the same way: a search of crates/ for refs/athena, update_ref or keep-around found nothing. timeout_seed falls back to the kept directory or to the base when rev_parse fails, and D151's Tradeoff states this.

summary: The change does what was asked. When the producer reaches its deadline, its changed files are now committed as a candidate, using the same build_candidate code as every other candidate. That candidate is recorded in candidate.json and in the outcome, and the job closes timed_out with a reason that ends "its edits are kept as candidate <short>". The progress note lists the changed files and the planned files that have no change yet. `athena retry` starts the next producer from that commit, and its "Resume" brief section names the earlier job and the candidate and quotes the note. I ran the lifecycle tests for keeping the work and for the retry, and the core timeout unit tests; all passed. fmt, clippy and the full suite passed in Athena's recorded CI checks. CHANGELOG.md has an entry, and docs/decisions.md adds D151, which cites D124 alternative (c) and lists the sources read. All findings are minor or nit. Two files outside the deliverables list changed, both small and needed. The change does not write a resume mark, which differs from the reading's wording but is reasoned out and fits the request. The kept commit is not on any branch, the same as other candidates, and the decision says so.
